thread:
mia: FYI noticed a sharp uptick in client-side memory growth and slow sparklines after last night's canary. charts hang for ~1.5s on some dashboards :eyes:
sam: Which canary? frontend or telemetry proxy?
mia: frontend canary that rolled the new asset-splitting heuristic (deployed ~23:40 UTC). small dashboards with many tiny sparklines are worst.
kevin: Saw similar on SLO dashboard. Heap climbs steadily until tab reload, then GC spike.
alexa: Repro steps? I can roll back if it's the split change.
mia: On staging I disabled the new splitpoint and issue went away. On prod we have a 10% canary still.
kevin: Profiling points to parse time in the chunk-loader + frequent eviction of the chart worker pool. suspect the new TTL for cached chunks is too short -> churn.
sam: Churn from chunk eviction would explain both CPU and memory (workers respawn). Any link to routing/kv cache changes?
mia: Platform routing changed affinity TTL on Tuesday to reduce hot-node pressure. That short TTL increases kvcache misses for charts that rely on same assets being reused.
kevin: tl;dr: splitpoint + short routing TTL = repeated chunk loads -> worker alloc + telemetry flood -> main-thread stalls.
alexa: Can we hotfix by bumping the TTL back and toggling the splitpoint off in canary?
sam: Yes. I'll open a rollback PR for the canary splitpoint now. Also propose to temporarily raise affinity TTL to previous value (300s -> 1800s).
deploy-bot: deploy request #1234 created by sam. Status: pending approvals.
mia: Also: telemetry sampling volume increased ~3x for chart-render events after canary (we emit per-chunk telemetry). Suggest we batch/aggregate on client before sending.
kevin: Agreed. Quick mitigation: debounce telemetry sends and switch sample-rate per-route. Long term: instrument a sentinel to track kvcache miss rates per-route and auto-slowdown telemetry.
alexa: Approving rollback. Can we coordinate with platform to bump TTL first so the canary rollback isn't the only change?
sam: I'll ping @kevin-platform for TTL change. If platform agrees we'll do TTL bump + canary rollback. Then follow with a telemetry debounce PR.
kevin: I'll draft an ops doc for safe TTL ranges and add a guard in routing heuristics so splitpoint rollouts measure kvcache miss delta before scaling.
mia: +1. Also add a telemetry tag so we can filter canary traffic in dashboards. Makes postmortem cleaner.
sam: Rolling plan: 1) bump affinity TTL to 1800s (platform) 2) rollback splitpoint canary (frontend) 3) deploy telemetry debounce patch (frontend) 4) follow-up: add kvcache-miss alert and guardrails.
alexa: I'll own step 2 and 3. Kevin, can you coordinate step 1?
kevin: On it. Will update once TTL change is live.
mia: Thanks all. Saving flame for postmortem writeup. :thumbsup:
